name: sample-3
description: Two pages of a 1914 letterpress novel, scanned at 600 DPI grayscale by Google and mirrored on archive.org. Single justified column of Latin prose, serif, running header, page number, end-of-line hyphenation. Public domain (archive.org: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT).
notes: The only Latin corpus here, and the reason it exists: PaddleOCR picks a
lighter recognition model for 'en' than for Chinese or Japanese, and the
--rec-model option that overrides that could not be measured without a
Latin page to measure it on.
No text layer at all, unlike sample-1 and sample-2, so force_ocr is false
and there is no incumbent variant to compare against.
Letterpress trap: in 'to help me escape' on page 1 the 'm' is printed from
a damaged sort and reads close to 'ine' at full resolution. The ground
truth says 'me', which is what a human reads; a recogniser that answers
'ine' is charged two characters for it.
The scan is 600 DPI, roughly twice sample-1 and sample-2, so a --dpi sweep
here is not measuring the same thing as a sweep on those.
